question: Who is the author of the book 'In an Antique Land'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Amitav Ghosh**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
__ 

• **Amitav Ghosh** is the author of the book "**In an Antique Land**," which was published in **1992**. 

• The book is a blend of **historical narrative** and **ethnographic study**, combining the genres of fiction and non-fiction. 

• "In an Antique Land" explores themes such as **cultural exchanges**, **history**, **identity**, and **migration**. 

• It is set against the backdrop of **Egypt** and **India**, focusing on the **medieval trade network** between these two regions. 

• Amitav Ghosh is an acclaimed author of several other novels, including "**The Shadow Lines**" and "**The Glass Palace**," which also delve into themes of history and identity. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
 

• **Amitav Ghosh:** 
 

• Amitav Ghosh was born on **11 July 1956** in **Calcutta, India**. 

• He is a recipient of several prestigious awards, including the **Padma Shri** in **2007** and the **Jnanpith Award** in **2018**. 

• Ghosh is renowned for his ability to weave **historical events** into compelling narratives, making him one of the leading authors in the genre of historical fiction. 
 
 

• **In an Antique Land:** 
 

• The book is a mix of historical research and personal narrative, offering a unique perspective on **cross-cultural connections**. 

• It is based on the author’s doctoral research at **Oxford University** and focuses on a 12th-century Jewish merchant and his Indian slave. 

• The book draws on the **Cairo Geniza** manuscripts, a treasure trove of historical documents preserved in Cairo's Ben Ezra Synagogue. 
 
 

• **Other Works by Amitav Ghosh:** 
 

• **The Circle of Reason (1986):** Ghosh’s debut novel, which won the **Prix Médicis étranger**. 

• **The Shadow Lines (1988):** A novel exploring the **partition of India** and its impact on families. 

• **The Ibis Trilogy:** A historical fiction series including "**Sea of Poppies**" (2008), "**River of Smoke**" (2011), and "**Flood of Fire**" (2015), centered around the **Opium Wars**. 
 
 

• **Neel Mukherjee:** 
 

• Author of novels like "**The Lives of Others**" (2014), which was shortlisted for the **Man Booker Prize**. 

• His works primarily delve into **family dynamics** and **social issues**. 
 
 

• **Manu Joseph:** 
 

• Known for his novel "**Serious Men**" (2010), which won the **PEN/Open Book Award**. 

• He frequently writes about **Indian society** and **politics**. 
 
 

• **Siddharth Dhanvant Shanghvi:** 
 

• Author of "**The Last Song of Dusk**" (2004), which won multiple awards, including the **Betty Trask Award**. 

• His works often explore themes like **love**, **loss**, and **identity**.
